chunks: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿUbayd Allah, from ʿAbd Allah al-Qaddāḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had struck another man until his sight was diminished. So he called for a man of his same age, then showed them something, and examined how much of his sight had decreased; then he gave him the indemnity for the amount that had been diminished from his sight.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in his role as the just ruler and judge
key_terms.دِيَةَ: financial indemnity owed for bodily injury

ai.seo_question: How is compensation determined in Shia fiqh when a person's eyesight is partially damaged?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding bodily injury affecting eyesight. It shows that compensation is assessed proportionally according to the measurable extent of the loss, reflecting precision and justice in diya for injuries to bodily faculties.
